See [the reusable kernel contract](kernel.md) for application ownership and the
non-research execution proof, and [installation boundaries](installations.md) for
independent records and runtime lifecycles. These remain inside this repository.

The local [improvement application](improvements.md) uses that same kernel contract
in an explicitly new experiment record. Captured public research informs code
proposals; it does not become writable research authority. Untrusted candidate
code runs only in restricted disposable containers, while the host scores its
outputs. An operator review receipt cannot apply code or grant release authority.

The [autonomous context lane](autonomous-context.md) is a separate WAKE application
policy on the existing per-node native authority. An installed capability permits
one selector-field change, gated by recomputed fixed-task and current-native-state
measurements. Proposal generation, adoption and rollback require no per-change
human review. Metadata events preserve research versions and history; candidate
data cannot replace the evaluator, widen permissions, modify code or create a
competing research store. Native replay owns the policy after restart.

> **Current specification.** This document explains why the present system is shaped this way: its trust boundary, durable record, governance model and known limits. Current local procedures belong in `standalone.md`; public mirror publishing belongs in `cloud.md`. Maintainer navigation, environment checks and reproducible validation guidance belong in `development.md`.

**WAKE✳︎** is infrastructure for continuity of accountable work, not continuity of a model instance. Its stable sequence is **Record → Context → Proposal → Governance → Transition → Receipt**. {"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=convergence+of+heuristic+search+models+under+high-uncertainty+epistemic+environments+consensus&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7612142\", \"title\": [\"Narrative Completion Under Uncertainty: A Synesthetic Provenance Architecture for Epistemic Transparency in Large Language Models\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Large language models generate outputs in which retrieved evidence, parametric memory, and generative interpolation are fused into a single undifferentiated text stream. The consumer of this output has no mechanism for distinguishing what was found from what was generated. This paper formalizes the problem as narrative completion under uncertainty and advances a falsifiable hypothesis: that the fused stream is nonetheless separable, because the boundary between evidential grounding and generative interpolation is geometrically decidable from transformer hidden states and the intensity of interpolation is quantifiable along a continuous gradient. The proposed instrument is a synesthetic provenance decomposition in which an auxiliary classification head, running parallel to the primary language modeling head, projects the shared hidden-state representations onto a continuous provenance gradient at every token position. Drawing on the linear representation hypothesis and the approximate orthogonality of semantic subspaces in highdimensional transformer embeddings, the paper proposes that provenance attributes are recoverable from the residual stream without distorting the geometry on which the primary unembedding head depends. The architecture produces a three-channel continuous signal analogous to RGB color depth, decomposing each token's generation into retrieval-grounded (R), parametric-memory (G), and generative-interpolative (B) components. The paper connects this decomposition to directed persistent path-homology and the complement set formalism for measuring structured absence, argues that the boundary between measurement and generation in LLM output is a continuous gradient rather than a discrete threshold, presents falsification protocols including dimensionality reduction stress tests against Cover's theorem, and specifies a concrete experimental proto…

{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=intrinsic+motivation+mechanisms+for+objective+discovery+in+reinforcement+learning&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1109/icdl53763.2022.9962187\", \"title\": [\"Getting Priorities Right: Intrinsic Motivation with Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1109/icdl53763.2022.9962187\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 9, 12]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.70675/6f863351zdd37z4da4z9fa2z5ceed27ddd07\", \"title\": [\"Learning increasingly complex skills through deep reinforcement learning using intrinsic motivation\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:title>Apprentissage de compétences de plus en plus complexes via l'apprentissage profond par renforcement en utilisant la motivation intrinsèque</jats:title>\\n                <jats:p xml:lang=\\\"fr\\\">En apprentissage par renforcement (RL), un agent apprend à résoudre une tâche en interagissant avec son environnement. Aﬁn de faire passer à l’échelle ces agents sur des tâches complexes, les méthodes récentes ont proposé avec succès d’intégrer les méthodes d’apprentissage profond au RL, créant le domaine d’apprentissage profond par renforcement (DRL). Cependant, la signiﬁcation sémantique d’une tâche est toujours pourvue par une fonction de récompense experte qui guide l’agent dans son processus d’apprentissage. Ce paradigme contraste avec la manière dont les animaux et humains apprennent: les travaux de psychologie suggèrent que les humains sont intrinsèquement motivés à acquérir de nouvelles connaissances à propos de leur environnement. Dans cette thèse, notre objectif est d’étudier comment la motivation intrinsèque permet de résoudre les problèmes expérimentés par le DRL. Tout d’abord, nous mettons en évidence comment les motivations intrinsèques actuelles attaquent certains problèmes du DRL. Nous classiﬁons et formalisons les méthodes, puis analysons leurs limites. Aﬁn d’exhiber leur importance, nous mettons en avant que ces verrous peuvent empêcher un agent d’apprendre des compétences et représentations de l’environnement de plus en plus complexes. Ce sont des éléments-clés pour faire apprendre des agents autonomes comme des humains. Á partir de cette analyse, nous introduisons deux nouveaux modèles qui peuvent…
